dedupe_keys.name: socioeconomic vulnerability and informal housing reconstruction in puerto rico after irma and maria

description: Hurricanes Irma and Maria caused widespread destruction in Puerto Rico in 2017, and in the absence of government recovery support, and with assistance denied on the basis of ownership, many households rebuilt informally. This study examines the individual and compounding effects of socioeconomic vulnerabilities on the likelihood of informal reconstruction, which offers an alternative path to recovery but carries safety risks and ambiguous legal status. The authors aim to identify households more likely to rebuild informally so that safe building practices and access to resources can be promoted, especially where informality is often seen as inevitable. Coverage: Puerto Rico. Access: article in Natural Hazards (2021), with a PubMed Central copy. Licence: none stated in the Europe PMC record. Caveats: findings rest on the households surveyed and the vulnerability indicators chosen. Simulation uses: household recovery pathways and assistance eligibility in housing recovery models. Related records: the multi-hazard Puerto Rico reconnaissance, FEMA IHP registrations and HUD CDBG-DR grants.
